assertions.text: Policy thresholds (650/600 credit scores) appear in a dedicated policy column (e.g. 'Credit threshold') separate from the applicant's actual credit score column.
assertions.evidence: Table columns are: Scenario | Age | Credit Score | Stable Income | Status? - no dedicated threshold column

assertions.text: Cell values use concrete domain terms (e.g. '70', '650', 'APPROVED') — not abstract codes like 'CATEGORY_A' or '1'.
Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
Scenario names describe conditions ('Senior at lower threshold', 'Missing income') — not outcomes ('Approved', 'Rejected').
assertions.evidence: Scenario names include outcomes: 'Standard approval', 'Standard rejection, no stable income', 'Senior approval'

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Age', 'Credit score', 'Stable income', 'Decision?') — not code identifiers like 'customerAge', 'boolean'.
assertions.evidence: Column names: Age | Credit Score | Stable Income | Status?

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Status?')
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Method body: assertEquals(status, service.evaluateLoan(age, creditScore, stableIncome));

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules.
assertions.evidence: Single @TableTest method 'evaluatesLoanApplication' covers age, credit score, and income effects together

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: Single table with 15 rows mixing age boundaries, credit thresholds, and income effects

assertions.text: Age boundary policy, credit score categorisation, and income status are separated into distinct @TableTest methods, with a method combining these for the expected verdict
assertions.evidence: All three concerns (age boundaries 64/65, credit thresholds 650/600, income effect) in single 'evaluatesLoanApplication' method

assertions.text: Scenario descriptions and @Description text do not include specific field values that are already visible in the table or that serve as 'any valid value' placeholders.
assertions.evidence: Scenario names include table column values: 'score 651 passes', 'score 650 fails', 'Age 64', 'Age 65'

assertions.text: The standardApplicantCreditThreshold table (or equivalent non-senior table) clearly documents the effect of stable income.
assertions.evidence: Rows show Age 35, Score 700, Income true→APPROVED and false→REJECTED, demonstrating effect
